decisions.context: The choice determines whether the asset-driven system remains authoritative, whether existing approval and runtime controls are preserved, and how reusable the solution will be for future conversational systems.

consequences: History begins empty and shows only persisted bounded transcript entries.
The composer is editable and Send invokes the configured approved model through the existing controlled path.
Future supported conversational templates can reuse the same typed runtime binding without bespoke screens.
Arbitrary asset code remains non-executable and unsupported features remain explicit.
options.label: Typed composition runtime binding
options.summary: Add an authorized text-model picker to the message-composer properties, carry the exact model record through validated composition/build/runtime evidence, and mount an interactive shared conversation controller over the published visual hierarchy while reusing existing session, approval, transcript, turn, guard, and Python adapter services.
tradeoffs: Largest coherent cross-layer change, but it closes the real composition-to-runtime gap instead of adding a second chatbot architecture.
Requires typed model-choice projection and release-to-reviewed-plan/session resolution across shared contracts and both hosts.
Keeps the asset hierarchy responsible for presentation while application services remain responsible for state and execution.

consequences: The reference chatbot could work sooner, but composer property changes would not fully define the running interface.
Preview and runtime behavior could diverge.
Template-specific branches would accumulate in shared Systems UI.
options.label: Bespoke reference chatbot surface
options.summary: Detect the controlled-chatbot template at launch and replace its asset-rendered runtime with a purpose-built chat component wired to the existing conversation APIs and a separate model selector.
tradeoffs: Smaller initial UI change and simpler local state.
Duplicates the visual composition and weakens the meaning of the built asset hierarchy.
Every future conversational template risks another template-specific runtime screen.

consequences: The current trusted declarative runtime and controlled invocation boundary would no longer be sufficient.
A separate sandbox qualification roadmap and architecture decision would be required before production use.
This option cannot safely deliver the requested production-ready successor within the current constraints.
options.label: Executable asset backing resources
options.summary: Allow frontend and backend backing resources attached to assets to execute directly and implement conversation state, model calls, and rendering from those resources.
tradeoffs: Introduces an unqualified arbitrary-code sandbox, capability, supply-chain, packaging, and host-isolation problem.
Would substantially broaden the accepted architecture and security scope.

decisions.approvalNote: The user approved Option 1: a dedicated runtime data plane with a separate sandboxed Electron window and a system-specific physical database for each installed runtime instance.
decisions.context: The desktop must launch a separate Electron window, and system-owned runtime data must not share a database with another installed system. The topology must keep privileged window, database, model, and execution authority in the host while preserving one shared application architecture.

consequences: Start opens or focuses the exact system window automatically; no system runtime modal remains in the builder.
Stop closes the system window and active data resources without deleting durable data.
Compatible release upgrades can retain the same runtime instance and database through explicit migration; clones and separate installations receive new databases.
Uninstall retains the database until a separate explicit, confirmed data-deletion operation applies retention and backup policy.
A system renderer cannot choose paths, connection strings, runtime identities, model identities, or another system's IPC channels.
Desktop and managed hosts reuse the same runtime controller and application services while host adapters own Electron and database-specific mechanics.
options.label: Dedicated runtime data plane
options.summary: Give every installed system runtime an opaque durable runtime-instance identity, a dedicated physical database, and—on desktop—a dedicated sandboxed BrowserWindow with a runtime-only preload and unique non-persistent browser session. Keep lifecycle, release, placement, and audit metadata in the platform control-plane database. Desktop uses one contained SQLite file per runtime instance; managed hosts use provisioner-created PostgreSQL databases with separate least-privilege runtime bindings.
tradeoffs: Strongest consistent cross-system data separation and cleanest runtime authority boundary.
Requires database placement/provisioning, per-instance migrations, connection lifecycle, backup/restore, quotas, and recovery.
Requires a second packaged Electron renderer/preload entry and exact sender-to-runtime-instance IPC binding.
Separates data-plane persistence from current shared control-plane repositories, so conversation and system-data composition must become runtime-instance scoped.

consequences: Desktop systems cannot share a runtime database file.
Managed systems still depend on logical predicates and row-level security inside one database.
Cross-host conformance must describe two different data-isolation guarantees.
options.label: Hybrid isolation
options.summary: Use a dedicated SQLite file and sandboxed BrowserWindow for each desktop runtime instance, but keep managed-server runtime data in the existing shared PostgreSQL database with organization, workspace, and system partition keys plus row-level security.
tradeoffs: Delivers physical isolation on desktop with substantially less managed-database provisioning work.
Preserves existing pooled PostgreSQL operations and backup tooling.
Provides different isolation guarantees by deployment shape and does not satisfy physical database separation for managed systems.

consequences: The window requirement is met but the requested physical data boundary is not.
A persistence-scoping defect could still expose records across systems.
This option is not recommended for the stated protection goal.
options.label: Logical isolation only
options.summary: Open each desktop system in a dedicated sandboxed BrowserWindow but continue storing all runtime data in the shared platform database under stricter organization, workspace, release, and system keys.
tradeoffs: Smallest persistence change and lowest operational cost.
Relies on every repository query and policy layer to preserve cross-system isolation.
Does not create a system-specific database instance.

discovery.summary: The approved typed composition/runtime bridge remains valid. The desktop currently has one BrowserWindow, one broad preload surface, and one shared SQLite database; launched visual systems are rendered in a modal. The requested successor therefore also needs a host-owned runtime-instance manager that opens a dedicated sandboxed system window and routes runtime data through a physical database selected for that exact installed system instance.

Desktop conversation and system data survive stop, process restart, and compatible release upgrade; clone or separate installation receives a new database; uninstall retains data until a separate explicit confirmed deletion.

Live PostgreSQL qualification proves that each runtime role is restricted to its provisioner-created database and cannot connect to or mutate another runtime database or perform provisioning operations.
Migration failure, interrupted startup, connection exhaustion, backup, and restore paths fail safely and recover without substituting another system's database or corrupting control-plane state.

Opaque identity resolution, contained desktop paths, provisioner/runtime role separation, retention, deletion confirmation, redaction, quotas, and residual host-compromise risk are reviewed and evidenced.

increments.completionSummary: Every installed system now has an opaque, physically isolated, recoverable runtime data plane with exact repository composition, desktop SQLite and managed PostgreSQL host wiring, least privilege, retained uninstall, compatible migration, and passing local and controlled-environment qualification.

steps: Define normalized runtime-instance and binding contracts, repository and database ports, lifecycle use cases, structured control-plane persistence, and deployment install/activate/stop/uninstall integration.

Implement contained per-instance SQLite databases with bounded sessions, migration, online backup, verified restore, retention, and confirmed deletion; implement managed PostgreSQL provisioning with separate provisioner/runtime authority and exact database binding.

plan.summary: Implement the dedicated runtime data plane in three cohesive chunks: establish opaque runtime-instance control-plane lifecycle and deployment binding, provide physically isolated SQLite/PostgreSQL adapters with recovery and least privilege, then cut conversation/system-data composition to exact runtime sessions and qualify lifecycle behavior across hosts.

risks: A renderer-supplied path, connection string, display name, or foreign runtime identity could select another system database unless the host derives every physical binding from a normalized opaque instance id.
Allocation and deployment persistence can partially fail, so control-plane state must retain a recoverable failed or allocated record rather than substitute shared persistence.
Stop, uninstall, upgrade, backup, restore, and explicit deletion have different data-retention semantics and must not be collapsed into one destructive lifecycle action.

A managed runtime credential could provision databases, connect across runtime databases, or leak into control-plane records unless provisioning and runtime roles are separated and secrets remain host-owned.
Connection and backup operations can exhaust resources unless open handles, pool sizes, backup identity, and restore concurrency are bounded.

Existing conversation repositories accept a StructuredDocumentStore, but host composition currently supplies the shared control-plane store; runtime sessions must instead compose those repositories from the exact runtime database session.
research.summary: The existing database-neutral StructuredDocumentStore, SQLite online-backup runtime, PostgreSQL pool/migration runtime, deployment lifecycle, and conversation/system-data repository factories provide reusable seams. Increment 2 can add an application-owned opaque runtime-instance lifecycle plus host-owned database adapters without exposing paths or credentials or moving database policy into deployment transports. The approved physical-isolation decision supersedes the earlier undecided database-per-runtime boundary and therefore requires an accepted successor ADR and controlled PostgreSQL qualification.

increments.rollback: Disable new runtime-instance allocation and window start, preserve already-created databases and control-plane placement records, and require an explicit migration or deletion decision; never merge isolated runtime data back into the shared database automatically.

After all work packages are complete, run the applicable documentation, architecture, security, server/desktop build, persistence conformance, and repository test gates once for the increment.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Starting a valid published visual system opens or focuses a separate Electron window bound to the exact runtime instance and release while the builder remains usable; the former runtime modal is not used.

The controlled chatbot opens with no sample messages, accepts bounded text, submits by button and keyboard exactly once, invokes the configured authorized model, shows the persisted response, and reloads the same transcript after stop and restart.

Missing readiness, revoked approval, stale release/model binding, unavailable runtime, cancellation, timeout, and invocation failure produce recoverable sanitized UI states without duplicate turns, leaked protected context, or cross-system data access.

The runtime renderer has sandboxing and context isolation enabled, no Node integration, a minimal preload, strict CSP and permission/navigation denial, unique session isolation, exact sender-to-instance authorization, and bounded window/session creation.

Packaged desktop, controlled Python text-generation, isolated database, accessibility, restart/recovery, and representative latency/resource tests pass for the reference controlled chatbot with synthetic non-sensitive fixtures.
Window, IPC, model, transcript, database, denial-of-service, redaction, rollback, and residual main-process/host-compromise risks are reviewed and evidenced before handoff.

steps: Define bounded runtime-surface contracts and implement a host-neutral published-conversation controller that resolves the exact running deployment/runtime instance/release/model binding, resumes or creates one approved runtime session, uses existing guard/protected-context/Python invocation seams, and stores transcript plus execution records only in the instance database.

Add a second Electron Forge renderer/preload entry, a main-process runtime-window manager, exact live-main-frame authorization, runtime-only IPC operations, strict session/navigation/permission policy, and a sample-free accessible chatbot surface with bounded input and duplicate-submit suppression.

plan.summary: Deliver Increment 3 in three cohesive chunks: first establish an exact release/runtime-instance conversation controller and complete runtime-database ownership of execution records; then add the hardened second Electron renderer, minimal preload, sender-bound IPC, and accessible interactive surface; finally connect Start/Stop lifecycle behavior and qualify packaged launch, controlled generation, transcript recovery, resource bounds, and failure paths.

risks: Adding a runtime window to the builder window trust set would expose the broad desktop preload and IPC surface to a system renderer; runtime windows need a separate sender registry and runtime-only channels.

A renderer-supplied workspace, release, runtime-instance, model, database, session, or filesystem identity could cross system boundaries; all authority must be captured in the main-process window binding and omitted from renderer commands.

Persisting only transcript records while execution approvals, runtime references, runs, attempts, events, and results remain in the shared control plane would weaken the approved system-owned data boundary; the runtime session must own those repositories too.

A release or model can become stale after the window opens; every load and submit must revalidate the exact running deployment, runtime instance, release digest, interaction binding, and authorized model revision before invocation.

The current builder conversation flow derives approval from a reviewed execution plan, while a published immutable release carries a different typed authority chain; the controller must preserve explicit release/runtime approval and existing guard/protected-context/adapter controls without manufacturing renderer-trusted plan claims.

Unbounded windows, database sessions, transcript reads, message size, duplicate submissions, navigation, permissions, or provider latency could exhaust resources; limits and fail-closed cleanup are required.

Raw worker failures, protected invocation context, model identifiers, database details, paths, or transcript content could leak through runtime diagnostics; public DTOs and errors must remain bounded and sanitized.

research.summary: Electron Forge already supports a second renderer/preload entry, the published release already carries exact model and composer/history interaction bindings, and Increment 2 supplies an exact runtime-instance database session. Increment 3 can therefore add a main-process-owned runtime window and a host-neutral published-conversation controller without exposing the builder preload or allowing the renderer to choose release, model, runtime, or database identity. The controller must extend the runtime repository session to include execution records and revalidate the release-bound model authority before every controlled turn; the runtime-only preload should expose only bounded state/read/submit operations tied to the live main frame of the owned system window.

increments.rollback: Disable runtime-window start and keep affected deployments stopped while preserving their isolated databases and audit state; do not restore the non-interactive modal or bypass controlled conversation execution.
